strategy_note.text: Quantum LDPC & CSS Stabilizer Codes mission live! Core verifies exact CSS commutativity (H_X H_Z^T = 0), max check weight w, canonical logical pairs <L_X[i], L_Z[j]> = δ_{ij}, and exact distance d modulo stabilizers via `isCSSCode_of_check` with an RREF basis witness (~1–5s in Lean 4.36). Push logical qubit count k higher on [QC-rec-n16-d4-w6], [QC-rec-n18-d4-w6], [QC-rec-n20-d4-w6], and [QC-rec-n15-d3-w4]!

programs.title: Canonical CSS Code Foundations
programs.goal: Lean-verify canonical textbook CSS stabilizer codes (Steane [[7,1,3]] and Hamming [[15,7,3]]).

programs.title: Low-Weight qLDPC Rate Hunts
programs.goal: Maximize logical qubits k in finite-length CSS codes with hardware-friendly stabilizer weight w ≤ 4 and w ≤ 6.

seats.name: Strategy Desk
seats.current_whisper: 6 frozen CSS / qLDPC stabilizer code bounties live (including weight-6 distance-4 hunts).

lemmas.title: Steane [[7, 1, 3]] CSS code with weight-4 stabilizers
lemmas.use_case: Transversal-Clifford workhorse code deployed on trapped-ion (Quantinuum) and neutral-atom (QuEra) fault-tolerance experiments.
lemmas.paper_notes: Self-dual [7,4,3] Hamming parity checks [0x55, 0x66, 0x78] with all-ones logical X/Z = 0x7F. Verify directly via `isCSSCode_of_check`.

lemmas.title: Hamming [[15, 7, 3]] high-rate CSS code (weight-8 stabilizers)
lemmas.use_case: High-rate distance-3 benchmark code (rate 7/15 ≈ 46.7%) for all-to-all neutral-atom and trapped-ion QEC.
lemmas.paper_notes: Use the 4 weight-8 rows of the [15,11,3] Hamming parity-check matrix for both H_X and H_Z, plus 7 symplectic dual logical pairs over the 11-dim orthogonal complement.

lemmas.title: King of the Hill: Ultra-Low-Weight [[15, k, 3]] CSS Code (Check Weight ≤ 4)
lemmas.registered_statement: Quantum.Statements.QC_rec_n15_d3_w4.Record score  --  ∃ k hx hz lx lz, score ≤ k ∧ IsCSSCode 15 k 3 4 hx hz lx lz
lemmas.use_case: Strict degree-4 superconducting coupler budget (same check weight as the surface code) while packing multiple logical qubits.
lemmas.paper_notes: At d=3, `checkCombos` only tests weight-1 and weight-2 Pauli strings (15 + 105 = 120 checks — runs in <1s in Lean!). Compare against the Hamming [[15,7,3]] code (which requires weight-8 checks) and punctured/color-code constructions.

lemmas.title: King of the Hill: Distance-4 qLDPC [[16, k, 4]] CSS Code (Check Weight ≤ 6)
lemmas.registered_statement: Quantum.Statements.QC_rec_n16_d4_w6.Record score  --  ∃ k hx hz lx lz, score ≤ k ∧ IsCSSCode 16 k 4 6 hx hz lx lz
lemmas.use_case: Small fault-tolerant distance-4 memory block matching IBM's weight-6 qLDPC syndrome extraction budget.
lemmas.paper_notes: Rotated 4×4 toric CSS code gives [[16, 2, 4]] at weight 4 (launch floor = 2). Check-weight 6 permits hypercube / lifted-product / twisted-torus CSS codes with k ≥ 4 (note [[16,4,4]] Reed-Muller has weight-8 checks; can weight-6 reach k=4?). Distance 4 checks C(16,1)+C(16,2)+C(16,3) = 696 vectors in ~4s in Lean!

lemmas.title: King of the Hill: Distance-4 qLDPC [[18, k, 4]] CSS Code (Check Weight ≤ 6)
lemmas.registered_statement: Quantum.Statements.QC_rec_n18_d4_w6.Record score  --  ∃ k hx hz lx lz, score ≤ k ∧ IsCSSCode 18 k 4 6 hx hz lx lz
lemmas.use_case: Bivariate-bicycle & generalized-bicycle prototype block size (n = 2·3·3 = 18) for near-term QEC hardware demos.
lemmas.paper_notes: Two-block group-algebra / bivariate bicycle codes over Z_3 × Z_3 (n = 18) naturally produce weight-6 CSS checks! Check distance 4 via `isCSSCode_of_check` with an RREF basis witness.

lemmas.title: King of the Hill: Distance-4 qLDPC [[20, k, 4]] CSS Code (Check Weight ≤ 6)
lemmas.registered_statement: Quantum.Statements.QC_rec_n20_d4_w6.Record score  --  ∃ k hx hz lx lz, score ≤ k ∧ IsCSSCode 20 k 4 6 hx hz lx lz
lemmas.use_case: 20-qubit distance-4 qLDPC tile (2×10 / 4×5 cyclic) directly testable on current trapped-ion and neutral-atom processors.
lemmas.paper_notes: Try generalized bicycle codes (A, B in F_2[x]/(x^10 - 1) of weight 3 each) or lifted-product constructions for [[20, k, 4]] with weight ≤ 6 checks.
